title: a test run from a linked worktree never casts a live ticket
assumption_check: Load-bearing: git reports a linked worktree's --git-dir apart from its --git-common-dir, and a main tree's as equal. Measured: Read 2026-11-14 on akienyoga9i, while building 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 (branch fixme-207c4074b3d5, 80246bd57): cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py:15 derives the store as <checkout>/../CairnCommons/tickets. On Windows every builder's worktree (C:/automation/local/cairn-<id>) is a sibling of the house commons, so that store resolves to the LIVE C:/automation/local/CairnCommons/tickets, in a git tree. red_tickets._rel keys a worktree's proof as inside its repo, and run_proof tickets every red. So a red-first `bin/cairn test` in a Windows worktree would cast a live ticket for a build in flight, and commit it into the house commons. This was read, not run: running it would cast the live ticket. On the Dell, /tmp worktrees have no sibling commons and hit StoreUnreachable instead (FIXME 1).
builder_check: D1: A LINKED WORKTREE NEVER CASTS. ticket_what_is_new asks git whether the repo it keys against is a linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`). If it is, the call casts nothing, commits nothing, and raises StoreUnreachable naming the worktree, so run_proof's FIXME 1 path prints '<proof> is red and was NOT ticketed: ...' and the run goes on. A proof's scratch repo, set through ROOTS['repo'] and made with git init, is a main tree and still casts, so 207c's teeth keep their world. Builds on 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 (StoreUnreachable). D2: PROOF, red-first. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_worktree_run_casts_no_live_ticket.py: a scratch main repo, a linked worktree added from it, and a scratch commons in git standing where the worktree's sibling store resolves. One tooth per clause.

collision_check: 207c4074b3d5 (FIXME 1, branch fixme-207c4074b3d5) writes red_tickets.py and device.py, so this builds on that branch and lands after it. 810fb2fc4a15 writes device.py declared_verbs, not the run_proof tail.
falsifier_check: 3 clauses: (1) a red run_proof over a proof in a linked worktree whose sibling ticket store is in a git tree casts no ticket and commits nothing to that commons; (2) the same run returns its red record and names on stderr that the red was not ticketed because the checkout is a linked worktree; (3) a red run over the same proof in the main tree still casts its ticket, so the guard is the worktree and not the red

bullets.text: On Windows a builder's worktree sits beside the live commons, so a red-first test run there casts and commits a live ticket; a linked worktree must never cast.
